RagShortTexts: Latgale routes linked lakes, woodland settlements and water crossings.
Travel through lakes and woods needed route and lodging knowledge in bad weather.

Latgalian hills, lakes and forests made households rely on both water and land. Carriers asked about crossings and lodging, while watchers noted approaching parties. Losing even a few boats or animals could alter a journey. Escorts checked whether boats could carry people, mounts, carts or sacks. Separate land and water parties needed agreed meeting points and carriers, not distance judged by eye.

Losing even a few boats or animals could alter a journey. Holding a lakeside post needed vessels, boatmen and supplies. Taking too many boats disrupted fishing and exchange, allowing short-term military needs to damage longer-term income.
